Unit Priority Stage 1
1 Costs
Tempo is the highest priority this patch so holds are all based on how likely they are to open up a win streak. Ravager is a trait that offers sustain making it great for long early game fights so Akali and Camille are S tier. They also can hold every offensive slam. Cinderling is the Premium AD backline holder, Karma is the AP counterpart. Rakan and Yorick are good 3 trait units, that will be useful in many lines, and the Juggernaut front line leads to a premium line. Rek'Sai and Kobuko are good for tempo but have less flexiblity. The Defender front liners are not bad but do not lead to any viable lines and doesn't enable fast 9 as hard as Juggernauts. Lower tier backliners are more conditional but can perform in the right set ups. For example, Xayah is generally not great unless you have a Guinsoo's and sufficient frontline. Varus isn't unplayable but requires multiple items that increase his casting output to be useful.
2 Costs
LeBlanc and Teemo are great AP holders and can perform in most circumstances but LeBlanc has an added bonus of providing econ. Scuttle Crab is a key hold as it enables the 3 Riftbeast opener a lot more than any unit other than Krug. Caitlyn is a great Guinsoo's holder and can enable fast 9. All 3 A tier frontliners are good in with their respective traits and very good if 2 starred. Murkwolf and Warwick are good when paired with Camille and Akali. Yunara opens up 3 Blossom that can be used for Econ or Yunara reroll, making her a great alternative if your spot lacks direction. Lower tier units are usable within the right context but are outclassed. For example, 3 Inferno can be used to cheat out higher cost units so if you must loss streak Shen can be valuable.
3 Costs
Kha'Zix from a 2-1 orb leads to a premium reroll line, if you have a Kha'Zix and a slam, heavily consider Kha'Zix Reroll . Even if you are not playing around Kha'Zix as a main carry his access to specific traits can be valuable later. Cassio is a premium AP holder that scales in longer fights which are very common in the early game. Krug enables a 3 Riftbeast opener, protects melee carries with his taunt on death, and is very tanky. Diana deals a lot of damage and opens up 4 Ravager. Azir is a premium reroll line but without a slam it is hard to justify holding him. Rengar farms money and holds every AD item in the game decently, making him great for any AD line. B Tier front liners are fine and useful if their traits are active. Yi and Kog'Maw are alright but out classed. Tristana and Mama Beak need Guinsoo's and are underwhelming.
Lose Streak

No/weak direction
No or low upgrade count
An econ augment
How to Lose Streak
Loss streak is not great at the moment. There are no reliable ways to cap out and win the game from loss streak and you will to high rollers if you bleed too much HP early on.
The only 3 reliable game plans from a weak opener are to either take an econ augment on 2-1, having some sort of condition that allows you to hard stabilize on stage 4 and play for top 4, mainly emblems or a Solar line. If you have to play a Solar line you need to find a way to save HP on stages 3 and 4 so you don't die to a highroll fast 9 player.
Coven isn't terrible and worth playing if you natural into it, but it is not as powerful as older iterations of econ traits. If you have it, play it but don't worry too much about keeping your loss streak solely due to Coven.
Full loss streak is generally not good, instead look to mix streak most of the time. If you are forced to full loss, try to farm at least 1 turn of 6+ loss.
If you are heavily loss streaking and you are not playing to spike very hard on stage 4 you are likely to bot 4. Most of the time if you are loss streaking and you don't have a special condition such as an emblem, it is advised to play Primal Malphite or Aphelios Flex , if you have to due to their strength through stage 4 and early 5. Nidalee is a great unit at winning stage 4 fights and stabilizing a bad game.
Lose Streak Comeback Mechanic
When playing loss streak your main advantage is carousel priority. This gives you 2 advantages, access to higher quality items, and the potential to high roll higher cost units that can be used for direction and stability. There is no need to slam subpar items if you know you are likely to lose fights anyway. Look to greed BIS so you can spike hard on stage 3 around a reroll carry or use your item quality to carry stages 4 and 5.

These sample boards are generically strong and can be flexed into different lines depending on your augments.

These boards can carry both an AD or AP carry easily. There are a lot of comps with duo carries in the meta at the moment so these flex boards hold for duo carry set ups extremely well.

If you choose to level it can play into any level 8 line or Fast 9 if you win streak for long enough. Akali can hold virtually any damage item in the game, preferrably AP, while Camille is one of the most consistent AD holders in the game. The front line can be any 2 piece you have upgraded. This is a very premium opener.

Leveling Guide
Leveling and Tempo are fundamental concepts to understand in TFT because they dictate the pace of your game. Leveling too early can cause you to have too little gold to roll with while leveling too late will cost you HP.
There are a few decision points when choosing to level.
How much money will we have left over?
Do we have to level and roll on the same turn?
What shop odds are we trying to optimize?
Can we preserve a win streak if we level?
General Tips:
Save gold if you need to
Roll at a specific level and you have NOT reached that level yet
You are healthy (high health compared to everyone else)
You have a strong board (you have key units, big synergies, unit upgrades compared to others)
Roll if you need to
Preserve your Health
Complete a lot of pairs (your bench is full of 2 copies of units and you need 1 more to upgrade a few of them)
Need units at a specific cost and you are at the optimal level to roll for them
Level up if you need to
Add an extra unit to activate a key trait (you may need to level up no matter what the cost)
Roll to obtain units at a specific cost (you will need to have enough gold to roll after spending gold on leveling up)
Have too much extra gold and you might as well buy XP
Standard Leveling (for Fast 8 or 9)
Win Streak (8+ Streak)
Round 2-1 2-5 3-1 3-5 (30g+) 4-2 5-2
Level 4 5 6 7 8 9
If we are winning, we want to push levels and access higher-tier units and continue our win streak. If we have a lot of pairs on 3-1, we are allowed to roll a few times to complete pairs. Same applies on 3-5. On 4-2 we are likely going to roll a little to stabilize and save some HP on the way to level 9. We aren't allowed to take 20 damage a fight stage 4, so you for sure roll a bit on level 8. Ideally, we hit a few 4 cost 1 stars, maybe a 5 cost or 2, and go 9 on 5-2. Sometimes we have to roll deeper and delay our 9 till 5-5. We want to leverage our HP from this spot and try to hit level 9 before other players. If you are streaking with an econ augment, you can even consider 4-5 level 9. Obviously win streaking is the best outcome because it gives you high health and so much gold, but we can't always have this happen, which means the games you do, you need to make the most of them.
Lose Streak (6+ Streak)
Round 2-3 (10g+) 2-7 3-2 3-5 (40g+) 4-1 5-2
Level 4 5 6 7 8 9
When we are lose streaking, we have to win out most of Stage 4, this means rolling a turn before tempo (4-1 on level 8) and doing our best to not lose a single fight this stage. Usually, off a loss streak, you are low health, playing at around a ~50-60 health deficit, so that means we will lose a life every time we lose a fight in stage 4. If you have a broken econ augment, you should structure your curve around leveling to 9 on 4-5, as the 5 costs are insanely strong and what will lead you to a first place comp.
Normal/Mixed Streak
Round 2-1 or 2-3 2-5 or 3-1 3-2 3-5 or 4-1 4-2 or 4-5 5-2 or 5-5
Level 4 5 6 7 8 9
Mixed streak is the hardest of all to play, as there will be a lot of nuance in minmaxing small amounts of gold from 2 streaks. The worst thing that can happen is LWLWL, but sometimes that is unavoidable. The hardest decision points will be leveling to 4 or 5 on stage 2. HP preservation is extremely important when playing mixed streak, as it is the only resource you have over the loss streak players. They are likely to outcap you, but you should have more lives than they do, and that can lead to them dying to other high-cap players while you coast to a 4th. You somewhat live or die by your 4-2 rolldown and hitting reasonable upgrades to save lives on Stage 4.
1 Cost Reroll
Do not press the level button at all until you 3 star your 1 cost.
Level 4 odds on 3-1 are very important as you are rolling at least a bit to stabilize and find extra copies. Depending on your econ, I like rolling to at least 32 gold because 32g > 40g > 50g, and you can choose to slowroll from there or dig deeper depending on your spot.
I personally like to aggressively roll on 3-5 because winning 3-5 and 3-6 is likely to give you an extra life, and 1 cost reroll does not cap as high as 4 cost and 5 cost boards. Most of the time, this spike in tempo ends up giving you +1 placement. 1 cost reroll is inherently more aggressive than a reroll of 2 or 3 cost, as it is cheaper to hold units, and you do not have to invest in leveling until you hit your desired units.
2 Cost Reroll
Lose Streak
Round 2-3 2-7 3-2 4+ 5+ 6+
Level 4 5 6 7 8 9
Other
Round 2-1 2-5 3-2 4+ 5+ 6+
Level 4 5 6 7 8 9
Level to 4 on 2-1 if you are strong/have a copy of the unit you are rerolling + a slammable item
Level to 5 on 2-5 if you are strong, if not make econ (20)
Level to 6 on 3-2 and roll to stabilize. You just slowroll from here.
Level 7 by 4-5 if possible
Level 8 5-2 if possible
3 Cost Reroll
Lose Streak
Round 2-3 2-7 3-2 3-5 (40g+) 5+ 6+
Level 4 5 6 7 8 9
Other
Round 2-1 2-5 3-2 3-5 or 4-1 5+ 6+
Level 4 5 6 7 8 9
Level to 4 on 2-1 if you are strong/have a copy of the unit you are rerolling + a slammable item
Level to 5 on 2-5 if you are strong, if not make econ (20)
Level to 6 on 3-2
Level to 7 3-5 If you have an econ Augment
Level to 7 4-1 and hit your carry 2-star to stabilize.
Hybrid 1 and 2 Cost Rerolls
These comps require you to 3 star both 1 and 2 cost units so the rules are slightly different from 1 cost and 2 cost reroll.
Our level of choice will be level 5 as it has the best odds for 1 cost that will be tricky to 3 star if we push at all.
Unlike 1 cost reroll, you can consider leveling to 4 on 2-1 as the 3-1 roll down is slightly less important, however this is only done if you can win 3 out of 5 stage 2 fights.
Round 2-1 or 2-3 2-7 3-2 4+ 5+ 6+
Level 4 4/5 5 6/7 8 9
Level to 4 on 2-1 if you are strong/have a copy of the unit you are rerolling + a slammable item
Do not level to 5 on 2-5 as it is often too expensive.
From 3-1 on you can dig to 2 star some pairs and then continue to slow roll for 3 star 1 costs.
Once you've hit most of your desired 1 cost, level to 6 and look for 2 costs, this will probably happen early stage 4.
Push levels around stage 5 after hitting all your 3 stars.
Strength of the Lobby
Knowing what people are playing is incredibly important, as it allows us to understand when they spike.
1 cost rerolls tend to spike at 3-1, 3-5, and 4-1.
2 cost rerolls tend to spike at 3-2, 4-1, and 4-5.
3 cost rerolls tend to spike 3-2, 3-5, 4-1, and 5-1.
Fast 8 players all spike at 4-2.
Fast 9 Players spike with fast 8ers on 4-2 and spike again on 5-2 when they hit 9.
This is incredibly valuable information because if the reroll players are in our pool, we would not want to expend resources to preserve a streak, as they will likely be stronger than us.
Say we are on an 8 streak on 3-5 with 50 gold. It costs 28 gold to go level 7 at the moment. Our pool is a 1 cost reroller a 2 cost reroller, and a Coven player.
If we take the information above into account, we should not level to 7 and instead make max interest as we are likely to lose to the 1 and 2 cost players and beat the Coven player regardless of what we do. A lot of people tend to force a level to be the strongest they can be to preserve win streaks, but it's not correct if you can reasonably deduce you will lose. In this scenario, you will lose 66% of the time unless you invest gold into rolling as well.
Knowing who is in your pool and when they are likely to spike is incredibly important to making the most out of our streaks.
